Jen — thanks for the clear list. Looping Marissa for legal detail but wanted to outline operationally what Redwood can commit to so you have something to share with procurement: 

1) SOC 2 scope: Redwood can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report that covers production systems (we do not include customer staging by default). We can provide a bridge letter for the period between report runs if needed.

2) Pen test: Redwood runs an annual third-party penetration test and a targeted internal test after major infra changes. For customer-facing evidence, we can provide a redacted pen-test summary, remediation timeline, and a short FAQ for findings. We typically do not provide full raw logs but can produce specific log extracts for agreed-upon scopes.

3) Audit / inspection rights: Our standard language allows for inspection with reasonable notice; 60 days is longer than our standard 30-day notice but we can accept 60 days for on-site visits for enterprise contracts (would need to be added to the order form as an exception). Sampled evidence for the last 12 months is feasible if the scope is limited to customer-affecting controls and we retain custody of data access records; otherwise we'd need a technical review window and a scoped list of items you intend to request.

4) Evidence cadence: we can commit to a quarterly evidence bundle (SOC-related items, pen-test summary, remediation status) uploaded to a shared S3 location or secure Google Drive folder. We'll also add a point-of-contact for evidence requests and a SLT escalation path if timeboxed requests are missed.

I'll attach a draft evidence matrix (SOC2_evidence_matrix.xlsx) that maps artifacts to SOC categories; Marissa/legal can work redlines into the MSA/Order Form.

Proposed next step: Marissa / Redwood legal to provide markup on the Order Form, and we can put the agreed exception language into a short addendum for signatures. If you want the 60-day inspection clause we can surface it as an enterprise exception tied to a contract value threshold.

Thanks,

Hi Jen / Soojin,

Thanks Jen  this is helpful. A couple of legal points from our side before we draft the redlines: 

- Audit rights: we cannot grant unbounded inspection rights or access to raw customer data. We can offer scoped, timeboxed inspections and agree on a sampling plan for evidence. 12 months of sampled evidence is acceptable where the request is narrowly scoped to specific controls (e.g., access change logs, incident reports) and is executed through our evidence ops process.
- Notice period: as Soojin noted, our standard is 30 days for inspection scheduling; we can accept 60 days as an enterprise exception. We'll call that out in the addendum.
- Pen test output: we'll provide a redacted report and remediation summary; full raw findings are restricted. We'll include language about redaction and confidentiality.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly upload is fine; we need to define retention and access (S3 pre-signed links with time-bound access preferred).

Karthik Iyer (legal) is on copy to finalize the MSA/Order Form language. Karthik, can you propose explicit clause text for: 1) Inspection rights and notice; 2) Evidence delivery cadence and retention; 3) Pen test deliverables and redaction/confidentiality?

If Helix can sign off on the operational matrix Soojin attached, we'll convert the Order Form redlines into a short addendum for signatures (keeps the MSA tidy).

Best,

Folks  following up with proposed contract language and a short rationale. I've attached a markup of the Order Form (MSA_security_exhibit_markup.docx) with inline redlines; below is a concise summary you can share with Helix: 

1) Inspection rights (proposed): "Customer may request a timeboxed inspection of Redwood systems limited to customer-affecting controls. Redwood will accept written requests with a minimum of thirty (30) days' notice; for enterprise engagements the parties may agree to an extended notice period in the Order Form addendum. Inspections will be conducted remotely by default; any on-site inspection requires mutual agreement and is subject to Redwood's onsite security protocols."

2) Evidence delivery & retention (proposed): "Redwood will provide a quarterly evidence bundle uploaded to a mutually agreed secure location (S3 or enterprise drive). Redwood will retain evidence artifacts for twelve (12) months from the date of collection unless otherwise required by law. Access to evidence artifacts will be provided via time-limited pre-signed URLs or secure transfer; raw logs will not be delivered without a separate court-ordered process or a narrowly scoped agreement."

3) Penetration testing (proposed): "Redwood will deliver an annual third-party penetration test summary and a remediation timeline. Reports will be redacted to remove vendor-sensitive items and customer-identifying data. Where customer-specific tests are requested, parties will agree on scope and deliverables in a separate statement of work."

Please note: the redlines preserve Redwood's standard confidentiality and IP protections while accommodating Helix's reasonable evidence requests. If Helix needs the 60-day on-site notice explicitly written, we can include that as a negotiated field under Section X (Order Form addendum).

I'll sync with Marissa to finalize and send a clean addendum for signature. Karthik will also provide a short one-page summary (FAQ) that the procurement team can forward to legal to reduce back-and-forth.
